I added `clever k8s version check` and `clever k8s version update`, but I haven't run any of it. `node_modules` isn't installed here, so `npm run fix-all` and `npm run validate` failed (`eslint: command not found`) and `node bin/clever.js` wouldn't start (`update-notifier` missing).

Before this is done, run `npm install`, then `npm run fix-all` and `npm run validate`. `fix-all` regenerates `k8s.docs.md` and the skill reference, and those aren't updated yet. Commit what it generates with the change.

The API client calls (`getK8sVersionCheck`, `updateK8sVersion`) and the helpers (`k8sCheckVersion`, `k8sUpdateVersion` in `src/lib/k8s.js`) already existed and nothing used them. The three new command files call those helpers:

- **`k8s version`** (`k8s.version.command.js`): a pure group with no handler.
- **`k8s version check <cluster> [--org] [--format human|json]`**: reports the installed and latest version. In human mode, when the cluster is outdated, it asks whether to update to the latest right away. That prompt comes from the existing helper, not from anything I added. `--format json` prints the raw check result with no prompt.
- **`k8s version update <cluster> [--org] [--target-version <v>]`**: updates to the given version. Without the option it prompts you to pick from the available versions. It fails if the version isn't available, and reports success without changing anything if the cluster is already on it.

I registered the group in `src/commands/global.commands.js`. All three commands use `since: null`.

I named the option `--target-version` rather than `--version` to avoid any clash with the global version flag. That's my choice, so say so if you'd rather have a different name.

I haven't touched `SKILL.md`, so check whether it mentions k8s commands.
